requirement: For an attention agent, since_s counts from the transition into attention; a re-notification while the agent is parked does not reset it. A waiting agent uses the other derivation.
why_it_matters: Confirmed by measurement against the real store (BACKEND-FINDINGS.md §1). The attention path bumps its last-seen column on EVERY re-notification with no state predicate, so deriving the wait from that column reports a true 600 s wait as 0 — and the queue's longest-wait-first ordering (§7) silently degenerates into time-since-last-re-fire, which is near-uniform across parked agents. The freshness bump itself must stay: over 900 s of silence is what makes an agent idle, so removing it drops live prompts out of the queue. Freshness and wait duration are two uses of one clock and are separated on the read side.

counterexamples.why: The agent has been blocked for ten minutes and reports a zero-second wait, because the re-notification at t+600 bumped the column the derivation read. It sorts to the BACK of the attention queue behind agents that have waited seconds. The shape is valid, so only this rule catches it — which is exactly how the defect shipped green in an earlier plan's test.
